topic: Design-stage minimax admissibility frontier for an external prognostic score of unknown quality. Finite population of n even units with FIXED potential outcomes; randomness is the assignment alone (design-based). Estimand SATE, estimator the design-unbiased difference-in-means, so with mu_i=(y_i(1)+y_i(0))/2 the exact risk is (4/n^2) mu' A_d mu where A_d=Cov_d(z). Design class D_n: all distributions on {z in {-1,+1}^n : sum z_i = 0} with E[z]=0, so A_d>=0, diag(A_d)=1, A_d*1=0; it contains complete randomization, every score-based stratified, matched-pair and rerandomization scheme, and all their mixtures. An external prognostic score, known for every unit BEFORE randomization and possibly miscalibrated or population-shifted, gives a fixed score subspace S (its score-derived span intersected with 1-perp), a PRIMITIVE known exactly at design time, with 1 <= dim S <= n-1. Score-quality class Y(rho,M;S) = {mu : ||mu||^2 = nM, ||P_S mu||^2 >= rho^2 ||mu||^2}; rho is UNKNOWN at design time (GSW JASA 2024 Sec 8: the analogous quantity 'cannot be directly observed or estimated in the design stage'). Determine V*(rho;S) := inf over d in D_n of sup over Y(rho,M;S) of mu' A_d mu, with an attaining design AND a matching converse over the full class D_n; and characterize the admissibility dichotomy A_n := {S : V*(rho;S) < V_CRD(rho;S) for some rho < 1} together with the threshold rho*(S) := inf{rho : V*(rho;S) < V_CRD(rho;S)} (=1 off A_n), including whether that characterization is computable from the score matrix alone. Also determine the finite-n additive regret R*(n,S) of a single design chosen without knowing rho. The unindexed minimax is degenerate (GSW Prop 4.2; Kapelner JSPI 2022 Sec 3.1); the score-quality indexing is what makes it nondegenerate. Exact enumerated witnesses: at n=8 with the pair-partition S, the matched-pair design has risk exactly 1.75x complete randomization on a legal mu that varies within pairs and risk 0 on one constant within pairs, so V*(1;S)=0<V_CRD(1;S)=4/7 and S is in A_n; and S=1-perp is NOT in A_n because trace n on an (n-1)-dimensional space forces lambda_max >= n/(n-1) with equality only at complete randomization. Functional forms, the value of rho*(S), the attaining design (pure or mixed), and any asymptotic formulation are delegated.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly which score subspaces S admit strict minimax improvement over balanced complete randomization at some rho<1, and give a score-matrix-computable formula or certificate for the threshold rho*(S).

source_refs.claim: The admissible correlation vectors of symmetric Bernoulli variables form a cut-polytope image, so positive semidefiniteness alone does not ensure assignment-covariance realizability.
source_refs.author: Mark Huber and Nevena Marić
source_refs.venue: Journal of Statistical Distributions and Applications

source_refs.excerpt: The EXACT zero/positive-loss frontier r_star ... is left as the honest OPEN object
Add explicit candidate formulas or named finite-dimensional dual programs for kappa_cut, r_cut, kappa_iid

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature supplies informative endpoints—rank-one prediction, scalar prognostic matching, and isotropic or permutation-symmetric classes—but no necessary-and-sufficient finite-n condition for an arbitrary subspace embedded in the balanced hypercube. The prior CausalSmith run isolates the same discrete-covariance obstacle in an adjacent design objective: its exact zero/positive-loss frontier remains open, and reviewers required explicit finite-dimensional dual programs. Dimension and ordinary eigenvalues do not encode how S meets the convex hull of balanced sign outer products, so a complete answer needs a geometric invariant of S together with a realizability certificate and a proved score-matrix algorithm or hardness result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient theorem for S to belong to A_n, an exact expression or finite optimization certificate for rho*(S), and an algorithm using only a basis or score matrix for S with a proved correctness and complexity guarantee.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing directly contrasts balancing prognostically useful directions with robustness to misspecification.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: covariate balance can improve precision -> restricted designs amplify error off the predictive span -> existing guarantees do not locate the transition -> which score subspaces improve minimax risk before perfect prediction?

method_exemplars.technique: Represent feasible symmetric-Bernoulli correlation vectors as a cut polytope and use the associated linear feasibility formulation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired threshold must distinguish abstract PSD covariance improvements from improvements attained by a genuine balanced assignment law.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce structured minimax design to spectral optimization over mixtures of balanced partitions and analyze rank-one versus permutation-symmetric endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The dichotomy interpolates between those endpoints and must convert spectral improvement into a realizable assignment mixture.

method_exemplars.technique: Approximate the Gram-Schmidt design by a skeletal process and prove a design-based CLT and limiting variance via exchangeable-pair Stein arguments and random-matrix concentration.
method_exemplars.why_closest: If an attaining design is GSW-like, this is the closest route from assignment-covariance geometry to a valid limit law.

open_problems.open_problem: For each balanced finite-population score subspace S and quality level rho, determine the exact value of V*(rho;S) over all balanced mean-zero assignment distributions, together with an attaining distribution and a converse over the discrete feasible covariance hull.

source_refs.claim: The paper gives the exact design-based MSE as a quadratic form in assignment covariance, but its finite-sample results are separate balance and robustness bounds rather than an exact score-quality-class optimum.
source_refs.author: Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Sävje, Daniel A. Spielman, and Peng Zhang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: For structured conditional-mean classes, the minimax design is a mixed-strategy optimal design; exact feasible-covariance optimization can require tractable inner and outer semidefinite approximations.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: A priori balance becomes minimax only after specifying structure linking outcomes to covariates; without such structure complete randomization is minimax.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.excerpt: Scoped out of v1: graph families beyond two-block, the fixed-treatment-count design class

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing exact minimax formulations mainly use ellipsoidal or RKHS outcome classes, where the adversary reduces to a largest-eigenvalue problem. The score-quality class instead imposes a lower energy share in S and forms a nonconvex spherical cone. In addition, feasible covariances are not all PSD matrices with unit diagonal and null vector 1; they must be convex combinations of zz' for balanced sign vectors. The prior CausalSmith implementability run explicitly scoped out this fixed-treatment-count geometry, confirming that its sign-symmetric two-block reduction supplies no converse here. Hence an SDP relaxation cannot by itself give either an attaining design or a matching lower bound over D_n.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact finite-n formula or finite-dimensional optimization characterization of V*(rho;S), a pure or mixed balanced assignment design attaining it, and a dual or extremal argument proving the same lower bound over all d in D_n.

writing_exemplar.why: Its zero-sum-game formulation moves directly from outcome structure to a mixed randomization distribution and separates exact feasible covariances from relaxations.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: complete randomization is minimax without outcome structure -> predictive structure can justify restriction -> score quality defines an intermediate structured class -> what is its exact mixed-strategy minimax value?

method_exemplars.technique: Formulate design choice as a finite zero-sum game, optimize over mixtures of balanced partitions, and use convex duality with semidefinite inner and outer approximations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired value is a worst-case quadratic risk over assignment mixtures, with a score-quality cone replacing an ellipsoid.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the exact assignment-covariance MSE identity, a martingale construction of the design, and design-based asymptotic normality with a conservative variance estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An attaining score-aware design retains the same difference-in-means estimator and assignment-only source of randomness.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the exact finite-n additive minimax regret of one balanced design chosen before the unknown score quality rho is known, relative to the rho-specific oracle value V*(rho;S), and identify an attaining design.

source_refs.claim: The GSW robustness parameter navigates balance versus robustness, but the Section 8 heuristic depends on predictive quality analogous to 1-R², which cannot be directly observed or estimated at design time.
source_refs.author: Christopher Harshaw, Fredrik Sävje, Daniel A. Spielman, and Peng Zhang
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The paper optimizes a rerandomization threshold by trading observed balance against unobserved-covariate risk, but the optimum depends on unknown outcome quantities and is computationally difficult even if they are supplied.
source_refs.author: Adam Kapelner, Abba M. Krieger, Michael Sklar, and David Azriel
source_refs.venue: Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference

source_refs.claim: Efficiency gains from an externally trained prognostic score depend on its predictive accuracy in the trial, so population-shifted score quality is a consequential unknown.
source_refs.author: Alejandro Schuler, David Walsh, Diana Hall, Jon Walsh, and Charles Fisher

source_refs.excerpt: Promote the asymptotic open question into a concrete theorem target by fixing a triangular kernel-menu class
No asymptotic limit law, universal kernel-menu rate, unrestricted global-balance theorem

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing balance-robustness procedures ask the experimenter to select a robustness or acceptance parameter, while the relevant score accuracy is a feature of unobserved potential outcomes. Unrestricted minimax analysis avoids tuning by collapsing back to complete randomization, and published minimax-regret experimentation work concerns enrollment or downstream treatment choice rather than selecting one balanced assignment law against a continuum of nested finite-population quality classes. The prior commitment-price run solves only finite direct-sum kernel menus; its reviewer explicitly requested a growing triangular menu, and its honest scope leaves universal menu rates and global balance open. The remaining obstacle is one feasible assignment covariance competing simultaneously with all rho-specific oracle benchmarks.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-n formula or exact convex-game characterization of R*(n,S)=inf_d sup_{rho in [0,1]}{sup_{mu in Y(rho,M;S)} mu'A_d mu-V*(rho;S)}, with an attaining rho-agnostic design and a matching lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It develops the balance-robustness tuning narrative and exposes why outcome predictiveness is unavailable before assignment.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: more score balance helps when the score predicts outcomes -> more restriction harms robustness when it does not -> predictive quality is unavailable at design time -> what single design minimizes regret against the rho-specific oracle?

method_exemplars.technique: Cast experimental planning as an oracle-relative finite minimax-regret game and solve for randomized optimal planning rules across heterogeneous regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its decision is sample selection rather than within-sample assignment, but its oracle-relative regret construction is structurally closest to optimizing one design across unknown rho.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent a randomized assignment law by a convex combination of balanced rank-one matrices and apply minimax and semidefinite duality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The regret problem is a zero-sum game over the same assignment-mixture polytope, augmented by oracle subtraction and a continuum of quality classes.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a tunable vector-balancing randomization, bound its exact design-based MSE through an implicit ridge criterion, and establish conservative design-based inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A regret-optimal design will likely mix or calibrate balance and robustness in the same assignment-only framework.

open_problems.open_problem: For the score-quality classes Y(rho,M;S), characterize the Pareto frontier between minimax quadratic risk and finite-sample randomization-inference capability imposed by a mass constraint max_z Pr_d(z)<=alpha/2.

source_refs.claim: Minimax precision need not ensure enough assignment uniformity for a Fisher randomization test, motivating an inference-constrained mixed-strategy optimal design.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: For SATE inference, the acceptable assignment set must be large enough for a nontrivial exact test; concentration on the best allocation pair can give low variance but essentially no randomization-test power.
source_refs.author: Per Johansson, Donald B. Rubin, and Mårten Schultzberg
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: Rerandomization yields a design-based limit law combining Gaussian and truncated-Gaussian components, so complete-randomization inference can be conservative.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li, Peng Ding, and Donald B. Rubin
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

open_problems.why_unsolved: Kallus gives an inference-constrained mixed-strategy design for ellipsoidal outcome structure, while the score-quality family is nonellipsoidal and its oracle varies with rho. Johansson, Rubin, and Schultzberg show that assignment support is a genuine finite-sample inferential constraint, and Li, Ding, and Rubin show that restriction changes the limiting law. No result gives the exact extra score-quality risk required to retain a prescribed smallest attainable p-value, or determines whether a rho-specific risk optimizer already satisfies the needed assignment-mass bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp finite-n value function for minimum worst-case score-quality risk subject to max_z Pr_d(z)<=alpha/2, an attaining design, and a converse quantifying the excess over V*(rho;S) as a function of alpha, rho, and S.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames precision and randomization-test capability as distinct design objectives and introduces the relevant assignment-mass constraint.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: structured minimax design improves precision -> an optimizer may concentrate on too few assignments -> exact SATE inference then loses attainable significance and power -> what is the score-quality risk-inference frontier?

method_exemplars.technique: Add coordinatewise mass caps to the mixed-design minimax program and derive semidefinite approximations supported on enumerated high-quality assignments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested frontier uses the same uniformity constraint but replaces an ellipsoidal kernel class with Y(rho,M;S).

method_exemplars.technique: Relate acceptable-set cardinality to the smallest attainable Fisher p-value and compare exact randomization tests with design-specific asymptotics.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the finite-support inferential criterion that the new minimax frontier must honor.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive the conditional finite-population limit law under rerandomization and invert the Gaussian-plus-truncated-Gaussian law for design-aware inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A score-balanced acceptance design may require the same non-Gaussian limit theory rather than complete-randomization standard errors.

literature_map:
1. Harshaw, Sävje, Spielman, and Zhang (JASA 2024, arXiv:1911.03071) formalize balance versus robustness through assignment-covariance operator norms, give the exact quadratic MSE identity, and leave tuning tied to unobserved predictive quality.
2. Kallus (JRSSB 2018, arXiv:1312.0531) establishes the no-free-lunch result without outcome structure and develops pure- and mixed-strategy minimax designs under structured outcome classes.
3. Kallus (JRSSB 2021, arXiv:2005.03151) proves that the exact optimizer is a randomized MSOD, exposes feasible-covariance optimization and SDP relaxations, and adds inference-uniformity constraints.
4. Kapelner, Krieger, Sklar, Shalit, and Azriel (American Statistician 2021, DOI 10.1080/00031305.2020.1717619) place a tail-risk optimum between perfect balance and complete randomization.
5. Kapelner, Krieger, Sklar, and Azriel (JSPI 2022, arXiv:1905.03337) tune rerandomization against observed and unobserved imbalance, but the optimum depends on unknown response quantities.
6. Morgan and Rubin (Annals of Statistics 2012, arXiv:1207.5625) introduce Mahalanobis rerandomization and connect variance reduction to R² and the acceptance threshold.
7. Li, Ding, and Rubin (PNAS 2018, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1808191115) derive the non-Gaussian finite-population limit law under rerandomization and design-aware inference.
8. Johansson, Rubin, and Schultzberg (JRSSB 2021, DOI 10.1111/rssb.12417) show that variance-optimal restriction may leave too little support for useful exact SATE inference.
9. Bai (AER 2022, arXiv:2206.07845) proves matched-pair optimality within stratified designs and isolates baseline-outcome pairing as a scalar-prognosis case.
10. Huber and Marić (JSDA 2019, arXiv:1706.06182) identify symmetric-Bernoulli correlation feasibility with a cut-polytope image, exposing the gap between PSD relaxations and realizable designs.
11. Wang and Li (Annals of Statistics 2022, arXiv:2109.02578) reconcile optimal balance and robustness asymptotically by shrinking the rerandomization threshold at a controlled rate.
12. Schindl and Branson (JASA 2026, arXiv:2403.12815) optimize quadratic-form rerandomization criteria and show that outcome alignment with the covariate eigensystem determines precision.
13. Guo, Liang, and Toulis (JRSSB 2026, arXiv:2502.16042) optimize Gaussianized assignment covariances and develop design-based confidence intervals, while using a continuous covariance parameterization.
14. Chatterjee, Dey, and Goswami (Annals of Applied Probability 2025, arXiv:2305.12512) prove a GSW CLT and limiting variance using a skeletal process and exchangeable pairs.
15. Schuler, Walsh, Hall, Walsh, and Fisher (IJB 2022, arXiv:2012.09935) show that external prognostic-score gains depend on in-trial predictive accuracy, highlighting population-shifted score quality.
